claim.signal: buy volatility-normalized dips (>=2 sigma below the trailing high) in a point-in-time wide-moat universe, expressed as long calls
claim.universe: point-in-time wide-moat screen on large-cap US equities, 38 names
claim.claimed_effect: dips in high-quality names can be bought profitably, with a long call as the defined-risk expression
claim.data_needs: daily option chains with IV and Greeks; point-in-time fundamentals

protocol.replication_anchor: re-derive contract counts and dollar P&L from primitives; rebuild the point-in-time universe from raw fundamentals
protocol.kill_criteria_for_the_claim: net-negative median trade after realistic option costs on the point-in-time universe, with non-recovering dips counted as prominently as recovering ones

verdict.outcome: NEGATIVE on the expression, not on the thesis — the long call loses $263 mean / $2,428 median per trade (win 0.36) while the same dips in the underlying are roughly flat to positive ($263 mean)
verdict.replication: accounting re-derived exactly (0 mismatches); universe screen reproduces 211/216 stored pairs

diagnostics.expression: option expression gives up $649 per trade vs the same entries in the stock; the call wins only 65% of the trades where the stock wins
diagnostics.volatility_prior_refuted: implied volatility rose rather than fell on recovering trades (mean +0.039 on trades exited >=30d from expiry; fell in only 23%)
diagnostics.option_clock: 247/282 (87.6%) of never-recovered dips returned to the entry price within 365d AFTER exit — the expiry clock, not the dip thesis (RECOVERED from the original session transcript, not locally reproducible; denominator verified against the trade record)
diagnostics.attribution: per trade, theta -$2,615 vs vega $1,825; in deep panics delta -$4,536 dominates (modelled levels, observed signs)
diagnostics.robustness: median negative in all 9 moat definitions; the mean turns positive only under the tightest screen (ROIC at least 18% in at least 80% of years, 1376 trades)

honest_limitations: the option-clock figure (87.6%) is recovered from the original session transcript, not recomputed here (needs the vendor platform); pinned in data/option_clock_probe.json, denominator verified locally; it measures recovery to the entry price so it is an upper bound, and it does not imply a longer-dated call would have profited
the delta/vega/theta decomposition is modelled and overstates P&L levels by $1,816 per trade; only its composition and its observed signs are relied on
the stock-vs-call comparison covers 1917/2392 trades (no exit price for positions closed at expiry)
deep-panic subsample is 48 trades; strike ordering is directional
moat screen uses restated fundamentals; costs use a modelled IV-scaled spread
